sites.name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)

sites.notes: Times: landing = LM touchdown, end = LM liftoff (Apollo Flight Journal / ALSJ).

sites.name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
sites.blurb: The only Apollo landing in the old, rugged lunar highlands.
sites.notes: Times: landing = LM touchdown, end = LM liftoff (Apollo Flight Journal / ALSJ).

sites.name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
sites.blurb: The last time people walked on the Moon, and the only geologist-astronaut to do it.
sites.notes: Times: landing = LM touchdown, end = LM liftoff (Apollo Flight Journal / ALSJ).

sites.name: Luna 9
sites.blurb: The first spacecraft to land softly on the Moon and send back pictures from its surface.
sites.notes: End time approximate (battery exhausted about 3 days after landing).

sites.name: Luna 13
sites.blurb: A Soviet lander that pushed a probe into the soil to test how firm the Moon's ground is.
sites.notes: End time approximate (date from sources, time of day unknown).

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.blurb: The first robot to bring Moon soil back to Earth.

sites.name: Luna 17 (Lunokhod 1)
sites.blurb: Home of Lunokhod 1, the first remote-controlled rover to drive on another world.
sites.notes: Landing site of Luna 17; end = last contact with Lunokhod 1 (approximate).

sites.name: Luna 20
sites.blurb: A robot that scooped up Moon rocks from rugged highlands and flew them home.

sites.name: Luna 21 (Lunokhod 2)
sites.blurb: Lunokhod 2 drove about 39 km here, farther than any other Moon rover for decades.
sites.notes: End = 11 May 1973 (date only; time of day set to 12:00 and approximate).

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.blurb: The last Soviet Moon mission; it drilled deep into the ground and brought a sample home.

sites.name: Surveyor 1
sites.blurb: America's first soft landing on the Moon, which sent home over 11,000 pictures.
sites.notes: End = end of first lunar day operations (approximate); sporadic contact until Jan 1967.

sites.name: Surveyor 3
sites.blurb: A robot lander that Apollo 12 astronauts later walked over to and visited.
sites.notes: End approximate (end of first lunar day).

sites.name: Surveyor 5
sites.blurb: A scout that tested the soil with a tiny chemistry lab near the future Apollo 11 site.
sites.notes: End approximate (last transmission mid-December 1967).

sites.name: Surveyor 6
sites.blurb: The first spacecraft to lift off from the Moon, with a short hop of a few metres.
sites.notes: End approximate (last contact mid-December 1967).

sites.name: Surveyor 7
sites.blurb: The last Surveyor, landed on a rugged highland near the bright crater Tycho.
sites.notes: End approximate (last contact 21 Feb 1968).

sites.name: Chang'e 3 (Yutu)
sites.blurb: China's first Moon landing, carrying the Yutu ("Jade Rabbit") rover.
sites.notes: End = Yutu declared dead (3 Aug 2016, date only); lander kept running longer.

sites.name: Chang'e 4
sites.blurb: The first landing ever on the far side of the Moon, inside Von Karman crater.
sites.notes: Still operating or end date not firmly known; end set to null.

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.blurb: China's sample-return mission, which brought home about 2 kg of young lunar rock.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.blurb: The first mission to bring back rocks from the far side of the Moon.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram)
sites.blurb: India's lander touched down closer to the south pole than any before it.
sites.notes: Site named Statio Shiv Shakti. End approximate (rover/lander put to sleep 2-4 Sep 2023).

sites.name: SLIM
sites.blurb: Japan's "Moon Sniper" landed within about 55 m of its target, though it ended up upside down.
sites.notes: End approximate (last operation Aug 2024).

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.blurb: The first private spacecraft to land on the Moon, near the south pole.
sites.notes: Coordinates from LROC-based reports near Malapert A (the Wikipedia object list shows a different value; low-medium confidence). End approximate.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.blurb: A private lander that worked a full lunar day in Mare Crisium and filmed a lunar sunset.
sites.notes: End approximate (shortly after lunar sunset, mid-March 2025).

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.blurb: The closest any lander has gotten to the lunar south pole, on a tall plateau; it tipped over.
sites.notes: End approximate (power lost within a day).
